title: Strict right-fibration slices compared naturally with intrinsic slices
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ and its coherent classification conventions of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], and strict right fibrations of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. For a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $D$, let $\mathsf R(D)$ be the simplicial category of $\mathcal U$-small strict right fibrations $E\to D$, with mapping Kan complex $\operatorname{Fun}_{/D}(E,E')$ of strict maps $E\times\Delta^n\to E'$ over $D$. Let $R_{\mathrm{int}}(D)$ be the full subcategory of the infinity-categorical slice $(\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U})_{/D}$ on arrows equivalent in that slice to strict right fibrations. Its arrows include the specified triangle homotopies. Sending a strict right fibration and its strict maps to the corresponding slice objects and maps induces an equivalence
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathsf R(D)\simeq R_{\mathrm{int}}(D).$$
Here $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ is the homotopy coherent nerve of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. In particular the comparison identifies the strict mapping Kan complex with the mapping space in the infinity slice. Strict pullback along $h:D\to D'$ corresponds under this equivalence to infinity-categorical base change along $h$. The strict-pullback assignment $D\mapsto N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathsf R(D)$ descends through categorical equivalences of base quasicategories, and these comparisons form a natural equivalence of functors $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U'}$. This includes arbitrary coherent transformations and all higher base simplices, not just strictly composable base maps. All slice and functor categories are formed in containing universes.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng Proposition 6.2, proof final paragraph (strict relative-category comparison); GHN Appendix A, Proposition A.30, Corollary A.32 and the right-fibration variant explicitly used there; Hinich, arXiv:1311.4128v4, Proposition 2.1.4 and its cartesian dual. This is only the strict/intrinsic slice comparison, not the classification by presheaves. Online sources read; archives WANTED. No Stacks tag.
